== con-leche/ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean#L90-L117
    90  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    91  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    92  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    93  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
    94  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
    95  `natOpPinSets`. -/
    96  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    97      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
    98      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins ds = .ok env) :
    99      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   100    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) rfl accepted
   101    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩
   102  
   103  open Frontend in
   104  /-- **The main corollary.**  A file declaring a theorem of type `False`
   105  in the shape `jsonWithTheoremFalse` describes is rejected: the parse
   106  reads the template's four lines into a theorem record of type `False`,
   107  the preparation keeps the record, and a stream holding it is never
   108  accepted.  At every pin list, as the main theorem: the shipped binary
   109  runs the fold at `natOpPinSets`. -/
   110  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   111      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (chunks : List ByteArray)
   112      (h : jsonWithTheoremFalse chunks) :
   113      ∃ e, (do
   114        let pre ← builtinPreludeE
   115        let r ← parseChunks chunks
   116        let ds := preparePrelude pre r.decls
   117        checkDecls .verified pins ds) = .error e := by

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/tagged.rs#L1-L20
     1  //! con-leche: none — the tagged counted handle of DESIGN.md §3.2 (task #94).
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::tagged` — **the crate's only `unsafe`, and it does not know what an
     4  //! `Expr` is**.
     5  //!
     6  //! One counted handle, one word wide, whose low four bits say which of a
     7  //! *scheme's* node types the rest of it points at.  Every block is allocated
     8  //! 16-aligned, which is what frees those four bits; sixteen kinds fit, and
     9  //! each kind's block is as wide as that kind needs rather than as wide as the
    10  //! widest.  That is the whole idea, and the measurement behind it is task
    11  //! #94's report: `Expr`'s nodes go from a flat 64-byte block to 32 or 48
    12  //! bytes, which is −45 % of Mathlib's peak.
    13  //!
    14  //! **This module is generic.**  It names no term type, no constructor and no
    15  //! kind: a *scheme* is a table, and [`tagged_kinds!`] turns it into the
    16  //! tag→type dispatch and the release.  `ron::node` is the one instantiation
    17  //! today (`Expr`'s ten blocks); `Name`, `Level` and `PropWhen` keep
    18  //! `ron::ptr::P` (DESIGN.md §3.2 — their nodes are not the bulk, and a
    19  //! uniform block costs them nothing).
    20  //!

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L87-L202
    87  const USAGE: &str = "\
    88  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
    89                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
    90                 FILE.ndjson
    91         con-ron --help
    92  
    93    (C), the Rust arena checker of con-ron's DESIGN.md section 8: con-leche's
    94    pure checker over an append-only DAG of per-constructor handle arrays, with
    95    con-leche's command line and con-leche's exit codes, so that
    96    scripts/diff-e2e.sh can run the same 383 fixtures against this binary and
    97    the Lean twin `con-ron-lean` alike.  A term is a u32 handle into a Vec: on
    98    the checking path there is no Arc, no tagged pointer and no reference count
    99    at all.  (The PINNED DATA the checker compares against is still
   100    con-leche's own constants as Expr values, interned into the persistent tier
   101    once at startup -- crates/con-ron-core/src/lib.rs says why.)
   102  
   103    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   104                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   105                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists), so a stream
   106                      declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.  What
   107                      the arena rewrite proves is that same statement about this
   108                      program's pipeline; the proof itself is phases P3 and P5
   109                      (DESIGN.md section 8.6) and is NOT done.
   110    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   111                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   112                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   113    --jobs=<n>        the check phase runs on <n> worker threads sharing the
   114                      persistent tier and the installed index by reference
   115                      (DESIGN.md section 8.3): each worker owns a scratch tier,
   116                      its own caches and a copy of the pin handles, and the
   117                      results are merged by record index and walked in record
   118                      order, so the verdict and the record a rejection names are
   119                      the same at every <n>.  Default: one per hardware thread,
   120                      capped at 16.  A worker reserves 1 GiB of stack, which a
   121                      `ulimit -v` must allow for.  0 or a non-numeral is a usage
   122                      error, as in con-leche.
   123    --no-mark-persistent
   124                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP, for a stronger reason than the
   125                      `con-ron` binary's: the mark it turns off is a
   126                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   127                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this checker has no
   128                      reference counts at all -- a term is a u32 handle into a
   129                      Vec and the persistent tier is immutable in phase B.  A
   130                      run that passes it says so on stderr.
   131    --progress[=<stride>]
   132                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   133                      phase:
   134                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   135                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   136                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> pending
   137                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   138                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   139                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s
   140                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   141                      declaration is installed, so a run that dies in the
   142                      install phase names the declaration it died in on its last
   143                      line; a check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th
   144                      COMPLETED check.  On a failure the phase's closing line
   145                      says so and the summary still prints.  Bare --progress is
   146                      stride 1; a stride that is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is
   147                      a usage error.
   148    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   149                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   150                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.  The pins
   151                      are interned into the persistent tier at startup, before
   152                      the fold (DESIGN.md section 8.6 P2d).
   153    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   154                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   155                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   156                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   157                      verified core and decoded by it.
   158    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   159                      position; no input is read.  Its last line names the
   160                      global allocator THIS binary was built with (below), so a
   161                      measurement can be reproduced.
   162  
   163  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   164  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   165  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   166  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   167  It is the same edge `crates/con-ron` has, so the two checkers are measured on
   168  the same allocator unless a build says otherwise.
   169  
   170  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   171  exits 3 without reading its input.
   172  
   173  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   174  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: this program aborts the way Rust aborts
   175  on a failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT,
   176  which a shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   177  
   178  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   179  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   180  built-in prelude's own records are not counted, and neither are the records
   181  the in-process modeller generates; a stream record that declares a prelude
   182  declaration IS counted.  That count is a property of the INPUT; the number of
   183  environment CONSTANTS is not.
   184  
   185  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   186  checker's own little prelude -- the six pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, PUnit,
   187  Empty, False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   188  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   189  the export chose.  It is parsed into the SAME store as the stream, which is
   190  what the persistent tier is for: the prelude's nodes and the stream's are
   191  hash-consed together.
   192  
   193  environment (con-leche's):
   194    CON_LECHE_INMODEL=0          turn the in-process modeller off; a mutual or
   195                                 nested block is then pushed bare and the FOLD
   196                                 declines it, having found no route
   197    CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS=1   report every mutual/nested block's outcome
   198                                 after the parse and stop (exit 2)
   199    CON_LECHE_PROJREC_TRACE      name each rewritten projection function
   200  These are the in-process modeller's debug switches and they go with it: no
   201  environment variable this program reads can shape a verdict, which is
   202  con-leche's own rule -- every such switch is a command-line flag.";

    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/node.rs#L1-L14
     1  //! con-leche: none — `Expr`'s instantiation of `ron::tagged` (DESIGN.md §3.2, task #94).
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::node` — **the ten `Expr` cells, as a table**.
     4  //!
     5  //! Until task #94 every `Expr` node was a `P<ExprNode>`: a block as wide as
     6  //! the *widest* `ExprKind` arm, plus a kind word, plus `Arc`'s two counts —
     7  //! 64 bytes for an `app`, which is 65 % of the live nodes of a real term
     8  //! (task #88's census) and needs 32.  Lean's own representation does not do
     9  //! that: the kind is in the object header, and each constructor's object is
    10  //! as wide as its own fields.
    11  //!
    12  //! So the kind moved into the handle, and `ron::tagged` is the machinery that
    13  //! puts it there.  **This file has no `unsafe` in it** — it is a table of ten
    14  //! `tag => variant: type` lines, ten struct declarations, and thin wrappers:

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/ptr.rs#L1-L8

     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::ptr` — **the one place the core names its shared pointer**
     4  //! (DESIGN.md §3.2, task #44).
     5  //!
     6  //! con-leche's terms are persistent trees with sharing, which the port gives
     7  //! reference counting: `P<T>` is the handle, and the model erases it
     8  //! (`Arc T := T`, plus four definitions).  Which *concrete* counted pointer

== crates/con-ron-core/src/kernel/expr.rs#L479-L495
   479  pub fn app(f: Expr, a: Expr) -> Expr {
   480      let df: u64 = data(&f);
   481      let da: u64 = data(&a);
   482      let h: u64 = hash32(name::mix_hash(
   483          17,
   484          name::mix_hash(hash_of_data(df), hash_of_data(da)),
   485      ));
   486      let d: u64 = pack_data(
   487          h,
   488          max_u64(bvar_of_data(df), bvar_of_data(da)),
   489          max_u64(fvar_of_data(df), fvar_of_data(da)),
   490          lp_of_data(df) || lp_of_data(da),
   491      );
   492      node::alloc_app(d, f, a)
   493  }

== crates/con-ron-dump/src/lib.rs#L155-L203
   155  pub struct MiMallocTight;
   156  
   157  #[cfg(all(feature = "mimalloc", not(feature = "jemalloc")))]
   158  unsafe impl std::alloc::GlobalAlloc for MiMallocTight {
   159      #[inline]
   160      unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: std::alloc::Layout) -> *mut u8 {
   161          if layout.align() <= 16 {
   162              libmimalloc_sys::mi_malloc(layout.size()) as *mut u8
   163          } else {
   164              libmimalloc_sys::mi_malloc_aligned(layout.size(), layout.align()) as *mut u8
   165          }
   166      }
   167  
   168      #[inline]
   169      unsafe fn alloc_zeroed(&self, layout: std::alloc::Layout) -> *mut u8 {
   170          if layout.align() <= 16 {
   171              libmimalloc_sys::mi_zalloc(layout.size()) as *mut u8
   172          } else {
   173              libmimalloc_sys::mi_zalloc_aligned(layout.size(), layout.align()) as *mut u8
   174          }
   175      }
   176  
   177      #[inline]
   178      unsafe fn dealloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, _layout: std::alloc::Layout) {
   179          libmimalloc_sys::mi_free(ptr as *mut std::ffi::c_void);
   180      }
   181  
   182      #[inline]
   183      unsafe fn realloc(
   184          &self,
   185          ptr: *mut u8,
   186          layout: std::alloc::Layout,
   187          new_size: usize,
   188      ) -> *mut u8 {
   189          if layout.align() <= 16 {
   190              libmimalloc_sys::mi_realloc(ptr as *mut std::ffi::c_void, new_size) as *mut u8
   191          } else {
   192              libmimalloc_sys::mi_realloc_aligned(
   193                  ptr as *mut std::ffi::c_void,
   194                  new_size,
   195                  layout.align(),
   196              ) as *mut u8
   197          }
   198      }
   199  }
   200  
   201  #[cfg(all(feature = "mimalloc", not(feature = "jemalloc")))]
   202  #[global_allocator]
   203  static GLOBAL_ALLOC: MiMallocTight = MiMallocTight;

   640  structure StateRel (st : cached.state_c.CState)
   641      (lst : ConLeche.Cached.CState) : Prop where
   642    ienv : HashMap.RelOn NameWF st.ienv lst.ienv absName absCConstE
   643    constTyAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_ty_at lst.constTyAt
   644      absNameLevels absExpr
   645    constValAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_val_at lst.constValAt
   646      absNameLevels absExpr
   647    ruleRhsAt : HashMap.RelOn NameNameLevelsWF st.rule_rhs_at lst.ruleRhsAt
   648      absNameNameLevels absExpr
   649    whnfCoreC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_core_c lst.whnfCoreC absExpr absExpr
   650    whnfC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_c lst.whnfC absExpr absExpr
   651    inferC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_c lst.inferC absExpr absExpr
   652    inferIOC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_io_c lst.inferIOC absExpr absExpr
   653    defeqC : HashMap.RelOn ExprPairWF st.defeq_c lst.defeqC absExprPair id
   654    annotC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.annot_c lst.annotC absExpr absExpr
   655    lsimpC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lsimp_c lst.lsimpC absLevel absLevel
   656    lnzC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lnz_c lst.lnzC absLevel id
   657    eqvC : HashMap.RelOn LevelPairWF st.eqv_c lst.eqvC absLevelPair id
   658    instC : HashMap.RelOn InstKeyWF st.inst_c lst.instC absInstKey absExpr
   659    /-- The `instC` table's **entry count**, which the other thirteen clauses do
   660    not need: `StateRel` is a lookup agreement and a lookup agreement does not
   661    bound the Lean map's size.  `cached::state_c::inst_list_m` is the one
   662    operation that reads a count — the `instC` entry cap, `inst_c.len() <
   663    inst_c_cap_c` against `mp.size < instCCapC` (`StateC.lean:186-199`) — so
   664    without this clause the two sides can disagree about whether the table is
   665    full.  Task #61 folded it in (`Refine/StateC.lean` had it as a free-standing
   666    `InstCSize` hypothesis that nothing could discharge). -/
   667    instCSize : (HashMap.al_v st.inst_c).length = lst.instC.size
   668  
   669  /-- The port-side invariant of the fourteen tables: each is a well-formed
   670  `ron::HashMap` (task #16's `Inv`) holding only well-formed keys and — where the
   671  values are terms — only well-formed values. -/

   895  theorem knot_induction {mode : env.CheckMode}
   896      (harms : ∀ fuel, Wrappers mode fuel → Bodies mode fuel) (fuel : Std.U64) :
   897      KnotSpec mode fuel := by
   898    have key : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ f : Std.U64, f.val = n → Wrappers mode f := by
   899      intro n
   900      induction n with
   901      | zero =>
   902        intro f hfv
   903        have h0 : f = 0#u64 := u64_val_inj (by rw [hfv]; rfl)
   904        subst h0; exact wrappers_zero mode
   905      | succ n ih =>
   906        intro f hfv
   907        have hlt : n < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := by
   908          have h1 : f.val < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := f.bv.isLt
   909          omega
   910        have hg : (Std.UScalar.ofNatCore n hlt : Std.U64).val = n :=

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/node.rs#L228-L263
   228  pub fn view(e: &Expr) -> ExprView<'_> {
   229      match e.0.tag() {
   230          TAG_BVAR => ExprView::Bvar(&e.0.cast::<NodeBvar>().i),
   231          TAG_FVAR => {
   232              let c: &NodeFvar = e.0.cast::<NodeFvar>();
   233              ExprView::Fvar(&c.idx, &c.ty)
   234          }
   235          TAG_SORT => ExprView::Sort(&e.0.cast::<NodeSort>().u),
   236          TAG_CONST => {
   237              let c: &NodeConst = e.0.cast::<NodeConst>();
   238              ExprView::Const(&c.n, &c.us)
   239          }
   240          TAG_APP => {
   241              let c: &NodeApp = e.0.cast::<NodeApp>();
   242              ExprView::App(&c.f, &c.a)
   243          }
   244          TAG_LAM => {
   245              let c: &NodeLam = e.0.cast::<NodeLam>();
   246              ExprView::Lam(&c.ty, &c.body, &c.m)
   247          }
   248          TAG_FORALL_E => {
   249              let c: &NodeForallE = e.0.cast::<NodeForallE>();
   250              ExprView::ForallE(&c.ty, &c.body, &c.m)
   251          }
   252          TAG_LET_E => {
   253              let c: &NodeLetE = e.0.cast::<NodeLetE>();
   254              ExprView::LetE(&c.ty, &c.value, &c.body)
   255          }
   256          TAG_LIT => ExprView::Lit(&e.0.cast::<NodeLit>().l),
   257          TAG_PROJ => {
   258              let c: &NodeProj = e.0.cast::<NodeProj>();
   259              ExprView::Proj(&c.n, &c.idx, &c.e)
   260          }
   261          t => crate::ron::tagged::bad_tag(t),
   262      }
   263  }

     6  //! the two phases with the boundary visible, the `--progress` heartbeat behind

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L49-L56
    49  //! **The verdict, and the record a rejection names, are the same at every
    50  //! `--jobs`.**  A worker's result is the record's index with its outcome; the
    51  //! workers' arrays are merged *by record index* into one table and the table
    52  //! is walked in **record order**, stopping at the first failing record in
    53  //! fold order.  That walk is `check_pending_list`'s, whatever the workers'
    54  //! timing, so the pool cannot report the second failure of a stream that has
    55  //! two — `pool_reports_the_first_failure_at_every_jobs` is the test, at 1, 2,
    56  //! 3, 4 and 8 workers on a list whose records 2 and 4 both fail.
